newsitem.title: USA: Dallas convenience store explodes, one killed.
newsitem.headline: Dallas convenience store explodes, one killed.

text.p: Explosions and fire raged through a Dallas convenience store early on Tuesday, killing one man and badly burning a teenager who was using a pay phone outside.
Fire Capt. Don Benda said the Kaybee's Grocery store in east Dallas was apparently rocked by three explosions shortly before 1 a.m.
The body of one man was found inside the store, which had already closed for the night, and Benda said it appeared to be the owner-manager.
Fire crews found a severely burned 16-year-old boy who told them he was using a pay phone at a corner wall of the store when the explosions began.

"It exploded and ignited him and he actually took off running. We tracked him down, he was running toward home to get some help," Benda said, adding that the boy was hospitalized with second and third degree burns over about 85 percent of his body.
Benda said fire officials were investigating the blast but noted that the store had cooking facilities which used natural gas.
